answer: A HESCO home in Hyderabad or lower Sindh using {{in.units|int}} units a month as an unprotected consumer on a {{in.sanctioned_kw|int}} kW connection pays about {{out.total_rs|rs}}: {{out.energy_rs|rs}} energy charge at {{out.rate|rs2}} per unit plus fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA and GST. HESCO bill = units × slab rate + fixed charge + surcharges + GST, with the month's FPA added from your bill.
how: {{out.units}} units × {{out.rate|rs2}} ({{out.category}} slab rate) = {{out.energy_rs|rs}}. Fixed charge for {{out.sanctioned_kw}} kW = {{out.fixed_rs|rs}}. FC surcharge {{out.fc_rs|rs}} + QTA {{out.qta_rs|rs}} + FPA {{out.fpa_rs|rs}}. Subtotal {{out.subtotal_rs|rs}} + GST {{out.gst_pct}}% ({{out.gst_rs|rs}}) = {{out.total_rs|rs}}.
key_facts: HESCO, the Hyderabad Electric Supply Company Limited, bills the uniform NEPRA A-1 domestic tariff for 2026; it has no rates of its own, so a HESCO bill for a given number of units equals a LESCO or IESCO bill apart from the monthly FPA line.
The HESCO per unit rate for an unprotected home using {{out.units|int}} units is {{out.rate|rs2}} on every unit, which gives {{out.energy_rs|rs}} before the fixed charge, surcharges and GST.

A HESCO consumer stays protected only while every one of the last {{d.protected_months|int}} bills is at or under {{d.protected_max_units|int}} units; in lower Sindh a single summer month with a fan-and-AC load above that limit moves the home to unprotected rates.

GST at {{out.gst_pct|int}}% is charged on energy, fixed charge and surcharges together, adding {{out.gst_rs|rs}} to a {{out.units|int}} unit HESCO bill; the surcharge and GST values are secondary-source figures that change over time.

The bill jumps at {{out.cliff_units|int}} units: up to there every unit is billed at {{data.tariff.unprotected.6.rate|rs2}}, but one unit more moves all of them to the top slab rate of {{data.tariff.unprotected.7.rate|rs2}}, which adds {{out.cliff_rs|rs}} to the bill of an unprotected {{out.sanctioned_kw|int}} kW home.

Income tax is not in this estimate: under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, a home not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays advance income tax of {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.rate_pct_non_atl|1}}% on a monthly bill of {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.threshold_rs|rs}} or more; consumers on the list pay none.

formula.text: Bill = units × slab rate + fixed Rs/kW × sanctioned kW + (FC + QTA + FPA) × units, then + GST
lines: slab rate = rate of the band the month's units reach (unprotected) or slab-wise (protected)
fixed = Rs per kW of the band reached × sanctioned kW
FC, QTA, FPA = per-unit surcharges printed on the bill

sections.h2: What is the HESCO per unit rate in 2026?
p: HESCO is the Hyderabad Electric Supply Company Limited, the ex-WAPDA distribution company with its head office at the WAPDA Offices Complex in Hussainabad, Hyderabad. It does not set its own prices. Like every other DISCO it bills the uniform A-1 domestic tariff that NEPRA determined and the Government notified for 2026. For an unprotected home the rate of the slab the month's units reach applies to every unit: {{out.units|int}} units are all billed at {{out.rate|rs2}}, which is why a few extra units at the top of a slab can cost far more than they look.

The worked examples and the table below print the rate for the protected, the mid-range, the summer-AC and the lifeline cases. Add the FPA from your own bill for the month's exact figure; it is the only line that is not in the uniform tariff.

sections.h2: Why is the HESCO summer bill in Hyderabad so high?
p: Lower Sindh has one of the longest hot seasons in Pakistan: fans run from spring to late autumn and an air conditioner can run from April into October. A home that uses under {{d.protected_max_units|int}} units in winter can pass five hundred units in a humid June, and because unprotected billing charges every unit at the rate of the slab reached, the energy charge grows faster than the units do. The third example below shows a {{ex.2.in.units|int}} unit month on a {{ex.2.in.sanctioned_kw|int}} kW connection at {{ex.2.out.rate|rs2}} per unit.

Protection is lost the same way. One month over the limit, including one stretched by a long reading cycle, moves the home to unprotected rates for the next {{d.protected_months|int}} months. If a HESCO bill covers more than a month of readings, check it with the overbilling check linked below before you pay.

sections.h2: Which areas does HESCO cover, and is Karachi included?
p: HESCO serves Hyderabad and the southern districts of Sindh, from the Indus delta around Thatta and Badin to the desert districts of Mirpurkhas, Umerkot and Tharparkar, and up the river to Jamshoro and Dadu. Karachi and its surroundings are not HESCO territory; they are served by K-Electric, which has its own calculator on this site. The districts of upper Sindh around Sukkur, Larkana and Khairpur were split off into SEPCO.

Whichever of the three companies sends your bill, the domestic slab rates are the same uniform tariff, so the estimate for a given number of units does not change; only the company name, the FPA line and the reference number do.

sections.h2: HESCO bill check: estimate here, read the printed bill on the HESCO site
p: This page is a HESCO bill estimate from your units. The official bill, with the reference number, due date, arrears and the exact FPA, is on HESCO's own website and on the online bill lookup that takes the reference number printed at the top of the bill. Use those to pay, and use this calculator to understand what each line should be, to plan next month, or to see whether a bill that looks too high sits in the slab it should.
For the full tool with every DISCO and a longer explanation of the slabs, see the electricity bill calculator for Pakistan linked below.

mistakes: Looking for a HESCO-only tariff. HESCO bills the uniform NEPRA domestic tariff; the slab rates are the same in Hyderabad, Lahore and Peshawar.

Ticking protected because the winter bills were small. Protection needs all of the last {{d.protected_months|int}} months under {{d.protected_max_units|int}} units, and one AC month in lower Sindh usually breaks the run.
Leaving the FPA blank when the bill shows one. The fuel adjustment is set every month by NEPRA and can swing the total either way; copy it into the advanced field.
Entering a bill that covers more than a month as if it were a normal month. A long reading cycle can push the units into a higher slab; use the overbilling check for those bills.

faq.q: How do I get a HESCO bill estimate from my units?
faq.a: Enter the units and the sanctioned load from your bill, tick protected only if the bill says so, and the estimate shows energy, fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA and GST. For {{out.units|int}} units the estimate is {{out.total_rs|rs}} before FPA.

faq.q: What is the HESCO per unit rate for a home?
faq.a: The NEPRA domestic slab rate for the slab your month reaches. An unprotected home using {{out.units|int}} units pays {{out.rate|rs2}} per unit; the table above gives the rate for each slab, and protected homes pay far less.

faq.q: Is the HESCO tariff different from LESCO or K-Electric?
faq.a: No. The 2026 domestic tariff is uniform across all ex-WAPDA DISCOs and K-Electric. The monthly FPA is the same national figure for the ex-WAPDA companies, so a HESCO bill and a LESCO bill for the same units should match line for line.

faq.q: What is the HESCO tariff for 2026?
faq.a: The uniform A-1 domestic tariff notified as SRO 279(I)/2026: lifeline slabs up to {{data.tariff.lifeline.1.upto|int}} units, protected slabs up to {{d.protected_max_units|int}} units, unprotected slabs of {{data.tariff.unprotected.0.upto|int}} units each up to {{data.tariff.unprotected.6.upto|int}} and an open-ended top slab; connections of {{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW and above are billed on ToU rates.

faq.q: How do I check my HESCO bill online?
faq.a: The printed bill, with the reference number, due date and payment status, is available on HESCO's own website and through the online bill lookup by reference number. This calculator estimates the bill from units; it does not fetch your account.

No. Karachi and the area around it are served by K-Electric. HESCO covers Hyderabad and the southern districts of Sindh; upper Sindh around Sukkur is SEPCO. The domestic slab rates are the same for all three.

faq.q: Why is my HESCO bill higher than this estimate?
faq.a: Usually the FPA line, arrears, a late-payment surcharge or a bill that covers more than a month. Enter the FPA from the bill in the advanced fields, and if the reading period is longer than a month run the bill through the overbilling check linked below.

faq.q: Why is my real bill higher than this estimate when it is over {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.threshold_rs|rs}}?
faq.a: A bill of {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.threshold_rs|rs}} or more a month carries advance income tax under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001: {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.rate_pct_non_atl|1}}% of the bill for a domestic consumer who is not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List. This calculator leaves it out because it depends on your tax status; check the income tax line on your bill and FBR's current withholding tax card.
